subject: Mobile Development
title: IBM Simon: The True First Smartphone
description: A tiny lesson with a big payoff: IBM Simon: The True First Smartphone.

hook.text: The first smartphone wasn't made by Apple. It was made by IBM in 1994.

buildup.text: The IBM Simon had a touchscreen, email, a calendar, and even a fax feature.

discovery.text: It cost $1,100, weighed 500 grams, and the battery lasted just one hour.

twist.text: Only 50,000 units sold. The world wasn't ready for a pocket computer yet.

climax.text: Simon proved the smartphone concept thirteen years before the iPhone existed.

punchline.text: IBM invented the smartphone; Apple sold it.

quiz.question: When was the IBM Simon released?
